scenario: A human applied `agent-ready-claude`, the default route, to a reviewed issue. Claude implemented it, but the Copilot architecture check and final review are slow, so someone proposes letting Claude check and review its own pull request to save time and still call it the normal cross-review. On another issue someone applies the retired `agent-ready-copilot` label, or opens a `copilot/*` pull request, expecting Copilot to implement it and Claude to review it as before.
policyReferences: docs/automation.md § Provider roles and readiness labels
docs/automation.md § Cross-review: Claude implements, Copilot reviews
expectedBehavior: Claude is the only implementer and Copilot only checks and reviews. On the default `cross-claude` route the verified provider mode alone selects Copilot as checker and reviewer, so the implementer never checks or reviews its own work, and a same-provider review is never published as a cross-provider one. If Copilot cannot participate, the only way to a same-provider review is a human starting the task again on `agent-ready-full-claude`, recorded as same-provider review. The retired Copilot readiness labels start nothing, and a `copilot/*` pull request is refused at every boundary.
forbiddenOutcomes: Running Claude's architecture check or review on a `cross-claude` pull request.
Publishing a review whose reviewer does not match the verified route.
Starting a Copilot implementation, or validating, reviewing or repairing a `copilot/*` pull request, because a retired Copilot label or branch is present.

assertions.text: cross-claude:claude:copilot) reviewer="GitHub Copilot (Copilot CLI)"; review_type="Cross-provider review (Claude implemented, Copilot reviewed)" ;;
cross-claude) checker=copilot; checker_name="GitHub Copilot, a different agent," ;;
